author: Kaup, 1847
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록
summary: 9월부터 이듬해 5월까지 여러 곳에 찾아와 겨울을 나며, 해마다 규칙적으로 오지는 않지만 천수만, 낙동강 하구, 해남 간척지에서는 비교적 꾸준히 관찰된다. 저습지, 호숫가, 넓은 갈대밭 같은 습지와 논, 풀밭 등 트인 땅에 살면서 물고기, 뱀, 개구리, 물새, 설치류 등을 잡아먹고, 갈대밭 같은 습지의 땅 위에 둥지를 튼다. 시베리아 동남부, 몽골, 우수리, 사할린에서 중국 동북부와 일본 북부까지 분포하며 한국, 일본 남부, 중국 남부, 동남아 등지에서 겨울을 난다. 몸무게는 370~780g이다.

sexes.female: 줄무늬가 있는 머리를 빼면 온몸이 밝은 갈색이다.

similar.how: 비슷한 곳에 찾아오지만 무리가 더 작고, 어느 지역에서나 관찰되는 수가 더 적다.

art.subject: Eastern Marsh Harrier (Circus spilonotus), adult male of the typical continental type, as seen over Korean reedbeds from autumn to spring: head, nape, throat and upper breast black streaked white, giving a dark hooded look; mantle and scapulars black mottled with white; folded wing with black primaries and silvery-grey secondaries and greater coverts, the forewing dark mottled white; rump white; tail plain silvery-grey; lower breast, belly, thighs and undertail white, the breast streaked black. Short hooked black bill with a yellow cere; yellow iris; long yellow legs.
art.pose: gliding low over a reed bed, searching for prey
art.scene: Korean winter wetland: wide reed beds beside a lake and open reclaimed farmland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on a reed tussock: black head and throat streaked white, black back mottled white, silvery-grey secondaries and black primaries on the folded wing, white belly, grey tail, yellow eye, long yellow legs
adult female, side view perched: dark brown body and wings, creamy-buff head and throat streaked dark brown with a dark patch behind the eye, rufous-streaked breast, grey-brown tail barred dark
art.build: Medium-large, slim harrier, 47–55cm long, a little smaller and lighter than Black Kite; females bigger than males. Small head with a slight owl-like facial disc. Bill short and strongly hooked. Long wings and a long, unforked tail; at rest the wingtips fall a little short of the tail tip. Legs long and slender, yellow. Flies low and slowly over reeds and fields, alternating a few flaps with long glides on wings raised in a shallow V.
avoid: Do not give the male a solid unstreaked black head, back and breast with a black bar across the wing coverts — that is Pied Harrier (Circus melanoleucos).
Do not paint a pale grey male with a grey head — that is Hen Harrier (Circus cyaneus).
Do not paint a broad-winged, short-tailed buzzard shape or a forked tail like Black Kite.
Do not paint the female's head plain dark brown; it is pale and streaked.
